\chapter{Complexity — Universal}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Universal
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module provides the universal Turing machine (Arora--Barak, Theorem~1.9
and \S 1.4.1): a single machine simulating any coded machine with
multiplicative overhead depending only on the code, the quadratic corollary
for total functions of arbitrary binary machines, and a time-bounded
(clocked) universal machine that reports success or timeout against a supplied
deadline.  Most declarations build the clocked simulator: a prefix parser that
separates the clock from the code, a table interpreter with exact step counts
that stops just before each simulated transition, a fixed-width binary
countdown, and an output-buffering wrapper that withholds emissions until the
simulated machine is known to halt in budget.  Throughout, bit strings are
written over $\{0,1\}$ ($1$ for true, $0$ for false); the \emph{pair encoding}
$\langle \alpha, x\rangle$ of two bit strings lists each bit of $\alpha$
twice, then the unequal delimiter pair $01$, then $x$ verbatim; and the
\emph{buffer tape} of a string $w$ is the two-way infinite tape holding $w$ in
cells $0,\dots,|w|-1$ and blanks elsewhere.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Linear-time universal simulation]
\lean{Turing.universal}
\label{Turing.universal}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.rightCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_of_halt, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.universalBlockBound, Turing.universalCanonTM, Turing.universalCaptureTM, Turing.universalCapture_interpreter_run, Turing.universalInterpreter, Turing.universalRelation, Turing.universalRelation_halt, Turing.universalRelation_output, Turing.universalRelation_start, Turing.universalSimulationCfg, Turing.universalStartupBound, Turing.universalTM, Turing.universal_from_blocks, Turing.universal_live_block}
\difficulty{4}
For every effective machine coding scheme $c$, there is a finite-tape machine $U$ over
the Boolean alphabet such that for every Boolean code word $\alpha$ there is a natural
number $C$ that works for every Boolean input $x$. If the machine decoded from $\alpha$
computes output $y$ on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$ computes $y$ on
$\langle\alpha,x\rangle$ in exactly $C(t+1)$ steps. Conversely, if $U$ computes an
output $y$ on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$ in some number of steps, then the machine decoded
from $\alpha$ computes $y$ on $x$ in some number of steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Quadratic universal simulation]
\lean{Turing.universal_quadratic}
\label{Turing.universal_quadratic}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.one_work_tape_binary, Turing.MachineCode.decode_encode, Turing.exists_codeTM, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.universal}
\difficulty{4}
Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme. There is a finite-tape machine $U$ over
the Boolean alphabet such that, for every finite-tape Boolean machine $M_0$, function
$f$ on finite Boolean strings, and time bound $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, if $M_0$
computes $f(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps for every input $x$, then there are a Boolean
string $\alpha$ and a constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every Boolean string $x$,
$U$ computes $f(x)$ on the paired encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$ within $C\,(T(|x|)+1)^2$
steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The stopped table interpreter]
\lean{Turing.timedCutInterpreter}
\label{Turing.timedCutInterpreter}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.universalInterpreter}
The four-tape table interpreter of the universal-machine construction,
modified so that every control state holding a fully decoded transition record
halts immediately instead of applying the record; on all other control states
its transition function agrees with the original interpreter.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Successor-preparation cost]
\lean{Turing.timedCut_NextCost}
\label{Turing.timedCut_NextCost}
\leanok
The number of interpreter steps used to decode a record's successor field and
install and rewind its unary state before the action is applied: $1$ for a
halting successor, and $2q + 4$ for a live successor of index $q$.

\begin{definition}[Physical clock prefix]
\lean{Turing.timedClockPrefix}
\label{Turing.timedClockPrefix}

The physical input region occupied by a clock string $b$ under the nested pair
encoding: each bit of $b$ repeated four times, followed by the four delimiter
cells $0011$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Layout of the nested input encoding]
\lean{Turing.timed_input_layout}
\label{Turing.timed_input_layout}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode, Turing.timedClockPrefix}
\difficulty{3}
For bit strings $b,\alpha,x$, the nested pair encoding $\langle\langle
b,\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$ is the physical clock prefix for $b$ followed by the pair
encoding $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Length of the clock prefix]
\lean{Turing.timedClockPrefix_length}
\label{Turing.timedClockPrefix_length}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.timedClockPrefix}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean word $b$, the physical clock prefix formed by repeating each bit of
$b$ four times and then appending $0011$ has length $4|b|+4$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Prefix-parser control states]
\lean{Turing.TimedPrefixControl}
\label{Turing.TimedPrefixControl}
\leanok
The finite control of the clock--code prefix parser: four phases that walk the
four physical copies of each clock bit, an end-of-clock phase for the
separator, and two phases that walk the doubled code bits.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The prefix parser]
\lean{Turing.timedPrefixTM}
\label{Turing.timedPrefixTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.TimedPrefixControl}
A one-work-tape machine over $\{0,1\}$ that scans the nested pair encoding
from the left: it stores each undoubled clock bit on its work tape (one write
per four input cells), then emits each undoubled code bit as output (one
emission per two input cells), and halts on the outer separator, before
reading any of the input suffix.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Prefix-parser configuration]
\lean{Turing.timedPrefixCfg}
\label{Turing.timedPrefixCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.TimedPrefixControl, Turing.pairEncode}
The configuration of the prefix parser on the nested pair encoding
$\langle \langle b, \alpha\rangle, x\rangle$ with a given control state and
input position, the captured clock string held on its work tape as a buffer
with head at the right blank, and a given accumulated output.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Value of a clock word]
\lean{Turing.timedValue}
\label{Turing.timedValue}
\leanok
The little-endian numeric value of a fixed-width Boolean word: the empty word
has value $0$, and the word with first bit $b$ and tail $w$ has value
$2 \cdot \mathrm{value}(w) + b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Value of the binary representation]
\lean{Turing.timedValue_bits}
\label{Turing.timedValue_bits}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.timedValue}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $t$, the little-endian value of the binary representation of
$t$ is $t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Fixed-width borrow subtraction]
\lean{Turing.timedBorrow}
\label{Turing.timedBorrow}
\leanok
Fixed-width binary subtraction of an incoming borrow flag from a little-endian
word: each output bit is the exclusive or of the corresponding input bit with
the propagated borrow, the borrow propagates exactly through the zero bits,
and the result is the final (underflow) borrow flag together with a word of
the same width.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Borrow with a clear flag]
\lean{Turing.timedBorrow_false}
\label{Turing.timedBorrow_false}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.timedBorrow}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean word, subtracting an incoming borrow flag set to false returns a false
final borrow flag and leaves the word unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Borrow subtraction preserves length]
\lean{Turing.timedBorrow_length}
\label{Turing.timedBorrow_length}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.timedBorrow}
\difficulty{3}
For every incoming Boolean borrow flag and Boolean word, the output word produced by
fixed-width borrow subtraction has the same length as the input word.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Borrow underflow criterion]
\lean{Turing.timedBorrow_underflow}
\label{Turing.timedBorrow_underflow}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.timedBorrow, Turing.timedBorrow_false, Turing.timedValue}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean word, subtracting an incoming borrow flag set to true produces a final
borrow flag equal to true if and only if the word's little-endian value is zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Borrow subtraction decrements value]
\lean{Turing.timedBorrow_value}
\label{Turing.timedBorrow_value}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.timedBorrow, Turing.timedBorrow_false, Turing.timedValue}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean word of positive little-endian value, subtracting an incoming borrow
flag set to true produces a word whose little-endian value plus one equals the original
word's value.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Timed-interpreter control states]
\lean{Turing.TimedControl}
\label{Turing.TimedControl}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.UniversalControl}
The finite control of the timed interpreter: a working copy of the table
interpreter's control, clock phases (rewind and borrow) that retain a selected
action's eight decoded bits and halting flag while the countdown is serviced,
an execute phase, and three output phases (emission start, buffer rewind, and
flush).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Six-lane assembly]
\lean{Turing.timedSix}
\label{Turing.timedSix}
\leanok
The assembly of a function on six tape indices from four core values, a clock
value, and a buffer value: indices $0$ through $3$ map to the core values,
index $4$ to the clock value, and index $5$ to the buffer value.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lifting an interpreter action]

\label{Turing.timedAction}

\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.timedSix}
The lift of a four-tape interpreter action to six tapes: the four core lanes
act as before, the clock lane is untouched, any emission is written to the
output-buffer lane (advancing its head) instead of being emitted, and a
halting successor is redirected to the emission-start phase so that the
machine stays live.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Timed administrative action]
\lean{Turing.timedAdmin}
\label{Turing.timedAdmin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.timedSix}
A six-tape action that leaves the four core lanes and the input head
untouched, performs a designated optional write and move on the clock lane and
on the output-buffer lane, optionally emits one real output bit, and passes to
a designated control.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The timed interpreter]
\lean{Turing.timedInterpreter}
\label{Turing.timedInterpreter}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.timedAction, Turing.timedAdmin, Turing.universalInterpreter}
The six-tape interpreter with a countdown clock: it follows the table
interpreter, buffering all emissions, until a decoded action is pending; it
then rewinds the clock lane and performs one fixed-width borrow pass.  A
successful borrow executes the retained action; an underflow halts the machine
emitting only the timeout tag $0$.  When the simulated machine halts, the
machine emits the success tag $1$ and flushes the buffered output before
halting.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lifting a four-tape configuration]
\lean{Turing.timedLift}
\label{Turing.timedLift}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.timedSix}
The six-tape configuration representing a four-tape interpreter configuration
together with a clock word: the four core lanes are copied, the clock lane
holds the clock word as a buffer with head at its right blank, the buffer lane
holds the four-tape configuration's accumulated output, and the real output is
empty; a halted four-tape control maps to the emission-start phase.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Agreement outside record states]
\lean{Turing.timedCut_regular}
\label{Turing.timedCut_regular}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.timedCutInterpreter, Turing.universalInterpreter}
\difficulty{2}
For any control state $q$ that is not of the form holding a fully decoded transition
record, and for every input symbol and four-tape read tuple, the stopped interpreter and
the original interpreter have the same transition action.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Backward Persistence of Liveness]
\lean{Turing.timedCut_live_before}
\label{Turing.timedCut_live_before}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.timedCutInterpreter}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x$ be a Boolean input word and $c$ a configuration of the stopped four-tape
interpreter on input $x$. For natural numbers $s\\le t$, if the interpreter has not
halted after $t$ steps from $c$, then it has not halted after $s$ steps from $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[No Pending Action Before a Live Endpoint]
\lean{Turing.timedCut_no_record}
\label{Turing.timedCut_no_record}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.timedCutInterpreter, Turing.timedCut_live_before}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x$ be a Boolean input word and $c$ a configuration of the stopped four-tape
interpreter on input $x$. If $s<t$ and the interpreter has not halted at time $t$ from
$c$, then at time $s$ its control state is not any pending-action state, for every
choice of the eight action bits and halting flag.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Core lanes of the six-lane assembly]
\lean{Turing.timedSix_core}
\label{Turing.timedSix_core}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.timedSix}
\difficulty{2}
Let $A$ be a type, let $a$ assign an element of $A$ to each of the four core indices,
and let $b,c\in A$. For every core index $i$, the six-lane assembly evaluated at the
corresponding index among the six lanes equals $a(i)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Applying a lifted action]
\lean{Turing.timedAction_apply}
\label{Turing.timedAction_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.timedAction, Turing.timedLift, Turing.timedSix}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, $c$ a configuration of the four-tape interpreter on
$x$, $clock$ a Boolean word, and $a$ an action of that interpreter. Applying the
six-tape lift of $a$ to the six-tape lift of $c$ with clock word $clock$ gives exactly
the lift of the configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $c$, with the same clock word.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One-Step Replay on Regular States]
\lean{Turing.timed_regular_step}
\label{Turing.timed_regular_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.timedAction, Turing.timedAction_apply, Turing.timedCutInterpreter, Turing.timedCut_regular, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timedLift, Turing.universalInterpreter}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a Boolean input, let $c$ be a four-tape configuration of the table
interpreter on $x$, and let $w$ be a Boolean clock word. If $c$ is live and its control
is not a state carrying a decoded transition record, then one step of the timed
interpreter from the six-tape lift of $c$ with clock word $w$ equals the six-tape lift,
with the same clock word, of one step of the stopped table interpreter from $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Replay of a Nonhalting Run]
\lean{Turing.timed_replay}
\label{Turing.timed_replay}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.timedCutInterpreter, Turing.timedCut_live_before, Turing.timedCut_no_record, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timedLift, Turing.timed_regular_step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a Boolean input, $c$ a four-tape configuration of the table interpreter on
$x$, $w$ a Boolean clock word, and $t\in\mathbb{N}$. If the stopped table interpreter's
configuration after $t$ steps is live, then the timed interpreter's configuration after
$t$ steps from the lift of $c$ with clock word $w$ equals the lift, with clock word $w$,
of the stopped interpreter's configuration after $t$ steps from $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Single active lane configuration]
\lean{Turing.timed_laneCfg}
\label{Turing.timed_laneCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape}
A configuration in which one designated work tape holds a finite zipper --- a
frontier position, a stack of processed cells, and a list of unprocessed cells
--- while every other component (the remaining tapes, all other heads, the
input position, and the output) is taken from a base configuration.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Single-lane action]
\lean{Turing.timed_laneAction}
\label{Turing.timed_laneAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
An action that writes an optional symbol and moves on exactly one designated
work tape, leaves the input head, the output, and all other work tapes
stationary, and passes to a given control state.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Reading the active lane]
\lean{Turing.timed_laneCfg_read}
\label{Turing.timed_laneCfg_read}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_read, Turing.timed_laneCfg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ and $S$ be types, let $x$ be a finite list over $A$, and let $base$ be a
configuration with $k$ work tapes. For a lane $lane<k$, an optional state $q$, an
integer frontier $z$, and finite lists $l,r$ of optional symbols over $A$, the
configuration obtained by replacing that lane with the zipper determined by $z,l,r$ and
placing its head at $z$ reads the head entry of $r$, or blank if $r$ is empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Right-moving zipper step on one lane]
\lean{Turing.timed_laneCfg_right}
\label{Turing.timed_laneCfg_right}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_right, Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.timed_laneAction, Turing.timed_laneCfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $base$ be a configuration with $k$ work tapes, choose a lane $lane<k$, optional
state $q$, state $q'$, integer $z$, lists $l,r$ of optional symbols, and optional
symbols $a,b$. Applying the action that writes $b$ on lane $lane$, moves that head one
cell right, and enters state $q'$ to the zipper configuration at frontier $z$ with left
list $l$ and right list $a::r$ yields the zipper configuration at frontier $z+1$ with
left list $b::l$ and right list $r$, state $q'$, and all other configuration data as
specified by the base configuration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One-lane finite-state transduction]
\lean{Turing.timed_lane_run}
\label{Turing.timed_lane_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.sweepFold, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.timed_laneAction, Turing.timed_laneCfg, Turing.timed_laneCfg_read, Turing.timed_laneCfg_right}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, choose a lane $lane<k$, and let
$R,C$ be types with maps $state:R\to S$ and $symbol:C\to A$ and a visit rule
$visit:R\times C\to R\times C$. Suppose that whenever the selected lane reads
$symbol(c)$, the transition from state $state(s)$, for any input and work-tape reads, is
the single-lane action that writes $symbol$ of the updated cell, moves that lane right,
and enters the state indexed by the updated register. Then, for any base configuration,
word $as$ over $C$, initial register $s$, integer frontier $z$, and lists $l,r$ of
optional symbols, running $M$ for $|as|$ steps from the zipper configuration whose right
list begins with the encoded word $as$ followed by $r$ yields the zipper configuration
whose frontier is $z+|as|$, register is the final register from the left-to-right
transduction of $as$, and left list is the reversed encoded rewritten word prepended to
$l$, with right list $r$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clock-lane administrative action]
\lean{Turing.timedAdmin_clock}
\label{Turing.timedAdmin_clock}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.TimedControl, Turing.timedAdmin, Turing.timed_laneAction}
\difficulty{2}
For any timed control state $q$, optional Boolean value $b$, and movement sign $d$, the
administrative action with successor state $q$, clock-lane instruction $(b,d)$, and no
buffer-lane instruction equals the single-lane action that writes $b$ and moves by $d$
on lane $4$ of the six-tape machine.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Borrow subtraction as a fold]
\lean{Turing.timedBorrow_fold}
\label{Turing.timedBorrow_fold}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.sweepFold, Turing.timedBorrow}
\difficulty{3}
For every incoming Boolean borrow flag and Boolean word, sweeping the word from left to
right with the local rule that sends a carry $c$ and bit $b$ to carry $c \wedge \lnot b$
and output bit $b \oplus c$ yields the same final carry and output word as the
fixed-width borrow subtraction.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Borrow phase over a clock word]
\lean{Turing.timed_borrow_run}
\label{Turing.timed_borrow_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.timedAdmin_clock, Turing.timedBorrow, Turing.timedBorrow_fold, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timed_laneCfg, Turing.timed_lane_run}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $c$ be a base configuration of the timed interpreter on
input $x$, let $u$ assign eight Boolean action bits, and let $h$ and $r$ be Boolean
flags. For every Boolean word $b_s$, integer frontier $z$, and finite lists $l,r_s$ of
possibly blank bits, running the interpreter for $|b_s|$ steps from the borrow phase
with flag $r$ and zipper state $(z,l,b_s\mathbin{+}r_s)$ yields the borrow phase with
flag equal to the final borrow from subtracting $r$ from $b_s$, frontier $z+|b_s|$,
processed stack the reversed resulting word followed by $l$, and unprocessed list $r_s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Tape Invariance Under a Frontier Shift]
\lean{Turing.timed_sweep_shift}
\label{Turing.timed_sweep_shift}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.sweepTape, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_read, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape_right}
\difficulty{4}
For any integer $z$ and finite lists $l,w,r$ of possibly blank Boolean symbols, the tape
represented with frontier $z$, left list $l$, and right list $w$ followed by $r$ is the
same function of tape position as the tape represented with frontier $z+|w|$, left list
given by the reversal of $w$ followed by $l$, and right list $r$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Buffer tape as a zipper]
\lean{Turing.timed_buffer_zipper}
\label{Turing.timed_buffer_zipper}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean word $b_s$, its buffer tape equals the zipper tape with frontier at
$0$, empty processed stack, and unprocessed list consisting of the bits of $b_s$ in
order.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Buffer tape as a processed zipper]
\lean{Turing.timed_buffer_zipper_end}
\label{Turing.timed_buffer_zipper_end}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.sweepTape, Turing.timed_buffer_zipper, Turing.timed_sweep_shift}
\difficulty{2}
For every Boolean word $b_s$, its buffer tape equals the zipper tape with frontier at
$|b_s|$, processed stack consisting of the bits of $b_s$ in reverse order, and empty
unprocessed list.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Clock-phase configuration]
\lean{Turing.timedClockCfg}
\label{Turing.timedClockCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.TimedControl}
The configuration obtained from a base six-tape configuration by overriding
only the finite control and the clock lane, whose contents become the buffer
of a given word with the head at a given position.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One clock-phase step]
\lean{Turing.timedClock_step}
\label{Turing.timedClock_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.timedAdmin, Turing.timedClockCfg, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timedSix}
\difficulty{3}
Let $B$ be a six-tape timed-interpreter configuration on a Boolean input word, let
$q,q'$ be timed control states, let $b$ be a Boolean word, let $p$ be an integer, and
let $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$. Suppose that for every scanned input symbol and every tuple of
work-tape reads whose clock-tape read is the symbol stored at position $p$ of the buffer
tape for $b$, the transition in control $q$ is the administrative action that enters
$q'$, moves the clock head by $d$, and makes no write or output. Then one step from the
configuration obtained by setting $B$'s control to $q$ and its clock lane to the buffer
tape for $b$ with head at $p$ equals the configuration obtained by setting that control
to $q'$ and moving the clock head to $p+d$, with the other fields retained.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clock rewind to the borrow phase]
\lean{Turing.timed_clock_back}
\label{Turing.timed_clock_back}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.timedClockCfg, Turing.timedClock_step, Turing.timedInterpreter}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a Boolean word and let $c$ be a base configuration of the timed interpreter
on input $x$. Let $u$ be a function assigning eight Boolean action bits, let $h$ be a
Boolean halting flag, and let $b_s$ be a Boolean clock word. For every natural number
$j\le |b_s|$, starting in the clock-rewind phase with clock word $b_s$ and clock head at
position $j-1$, after exactly $j+1$ steps the interpreter is in the borrow phase with
borrow flag true, the same clock word, and clock head at $0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Borrow pass over the clock word]
\lean{Turing.timed_clock_borrow}
\label{Turing.timed_clock_borrow}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.timedBorrow, Turing.timedBorrow_length, Turing.timedClockCfg, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timed_borrow_run, Turing.timed_buffer_zipper, Turing.timed_buffer_zipper_end, Turing.timed_laneCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ and $bs$ be finite Boolean words, let $base$ be a six-tape configuration over
input $x$, let $bits$ assign a Boolean to each index below $8$, and let $halt$ and
$carry$ be Boolean flags. Starting from the clock-phase configuration with control
$(borrow(bits,halt,carry))$, clock word $bs$, and clock head at $0$, after exactly
$|bs|$ steps the timed interpreter reaches the clock-phase configuration with the same
base data, control $(borrow(bits,halt,c'))$, clock word $bs'$, and head at $|bs|$, where
$(c',bs')$ is the fixed-width subtraction of the incoming borrow flag from $bs$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Entering the clock rewind phase]
\lean{Turing.timed_clock_start}
\label{Turing.timed_clock_start}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.timedAdmin, Turing.timedClockCfg, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timedLift, Turing.timedSix}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input word, let $cfg$ be a four-tape configuration over $x$,
let $bs$ be a finite Boolean clock word, let $bits$ assign a Boolean to each index below
$8$, and let $halt$ be a Boolean flag. If $cfg$ has the pending-action control carrying
$bits$ and $halt$, then one step of the timed interpreter from its six-tape lift with
clock word $bs$ reaches the clock-rewind phase carrying the same $bits$ and $halt$, with
the clock word unchanged and its head at $|bs|-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Complete clock countdown pass]
\lean{Turing.timed_clock_pass}
\label{Turing.timed_clock_pass}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.timedBorrow, Turing.timedClockCfg, Turing.timedCut_run_join, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timedLift, Turing.timed_clock_back, Turing.timed_clock_borrow, Turing.timed_clock_start}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input word, let $cfg$ be a four-tape configuration over $x$,
let $bs$ be a finite Boolean clock word, let $bits$ assign a Boolean to each index below
$8$, and let $halt$ be a Boolean flag. Assume the control of $cfg$ is the pending-action
state carrying $bits$ and $halt$. Starting from the six-tape lift of $cfg$ with clock
word $bs$, after exactly $2|bs|+2$ steps the timed interpreter reaches the clock-phase
configuration with control $(borrow(bits,halt,c))$, clock word $bs'$, and head at
$|bs|$, where $(c,bs')$ is the fixed-width subtraction of an incoming borrow from $bs$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Execution of a retained action]
\lean{Turing.timed_execute}
\label{Turing.timed_execute}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.timedAction, Turing.timedAction_apply, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timedLift, Turing.universalInterpreter}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x$ be a bit string, $c$ a four-tape interpreter configuration on input $x$, $b$ a
clock word, and suppose the control state of $c$ is the pending-action state carrying
action bits $a$ and halting flag $h$. If the six-tape timed interpreter is started from
the lift of $c$ with clock word $b$, but with its control set to the execute phase
carrying $a$ and $h$, then one step produces the lift of the result of one step of the
four-tape table interpreter from $c$, with clock word $b$ unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Executing a transition with positive budget]
\lean{Turing.timed_clock_success}
\label{Turing.timed_clock_success}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.timedAdmin, Turing.timedBorrow, Turing.timedBorrow_length, Turing.timedBorrow_underflow, Turing.timedClockCfg, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timedLift, Turing.timedSix, Turing.timedValue, Turing.timed_clock_pass, Turing.timed_execute, Turing.universalInterpreter}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input word, let $cfg$ be a four-tape configuration over $x$,
let $bs$ be a finite Boolean clock word, let $bits$ assign a Boolean to each index below
$8$, and let $halt$ be a Boolean flag. Suppose $cfg$ has the pending-action control
carrying $bits$ and $halt$, and the little-endian value of $bs$ is positive. After
exactly $2|bs|+4$ steps from the six-tape lift of $cfg$ with clock word $bs$, the timed
interpreter reaches the lift of one step of the four-tape interpreter from $cfg$, with
clock word the fixed-width subtraction of an incoming borrow from $bs$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Timeout at zero budget]
\lean{Turing.timed_clock_timeout}
\label{Turing.timed_clock_timeout}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.timedAdmin, Turing.timedBorrow, Turing.timedBorrow_length, Turing.timedBorrow_underflow, Turing.timedClockCfg, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timedLift, Turing.timedValue, Turing.timed_clock_pass}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input word, let $cfg$ be a four-tape configuration over $x$,
let $bs$ be a finite Boolean clock word, let $bits$ assign a Boolean to each index below
$8$, and let $halt$ be a Boolean flag. Suppose $cfg$ has the pending-action control
carrying $bits$ and $halt$, and the little-endian value of $bs$ is zero. After exactly
$2|bs|+3$ steps from the six-tape lift of $cfg$ with clock word $bs$, the timed
interpreter is halted and its real output is exactly the one-bit word $[0]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Output-phase configuration]
\lean{Turing.timedOutputCfg}
\label{Turing.timedOutputCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.timedLift}
The configuration obtained from the six-tape lift of a four-tape configuration
and a clock word by overriding the finite control, the output-buffer head
position, and the real output; all simulation and clock tapes are retained.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One output-phase step]
\lean{Turing.timed_output_step}
\label{Turing.timed_output_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.timedAdmin, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timedLift, Turing.timedOutputCfg, Turing.timedSix}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $c$ be a four-tape interpreter configuration on input
$x$. Let $b$ be a Boolean word, $q$ a timed-interpreter control, $q'$ an optional
timed-interpreter control, $p\in\mathbb{Z}$ a buffer-head position, $o$ a Boolean output
word, $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$ a head movement, and $e$ an optional Boolean. Suppose that for
every input symbol and every tuple of work-tape symbols, whenever lane $5$ contains at
its head the symbol stored in $c$'s output buffer at position $p$, the transition from
$q$ is an administrative action that leaves the clock lane unchanged, moves the buffer
lane by $d$, emits $e$, and enters control $q'$. Then one step from the lifted
configuration in control $q$, with buffer head at $p$ and real output $o$, yields the
lifted configuration in control $q'$, with buffer head at $p+d$ and real output $o$
followed by $e$, if present.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Output-buffer rewind]

Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $c$ be a configuration of the four-tape
interpreter on input $x$. For Boolean words $b$ and $o$, and a natural number $j$ with
$j\leq |c.output|$, start the timed interpreter in its output-buffer rewind phase, with
clock word $b$, the output buffer initialized from $c.output$ and its head at position
$j-1$, and real output $o$. After $j+1$ steps it is in the flush phase with the buffer
head at position $0$ and real output $o$ followed by the bit $1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Flushing the output buffer]

Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $c$ be a configuration of the four-tape
interpreter on input $x$. For Boolean words $b,r,l,o$ with the interpreter’s output

output-buffer head at position $|l|$ and real output $o$, after $|r|+1$ steps the
machine is halted, the output-buffer head is at position $|c.output|$, and the real
output is the concatenation of $o$ and $r$.
\end{lemma}

canonizer: the parser extracts the code string from the nested pair encoding,
and only that extracted code is supplied as virtual input to the canonizer.

\begin{definition}[The retained clock lane]

prefix parser's unique work tape, on which the extracted clock word is
retained.

position $4|b|+2|\alpha|+7$, buffer tapes containing $b$, and their heads at position
$|b|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Timed canonizer run correspondence]

\begin{definition}[Deadline-inclusive answer]
\lean{Turing.timedAnswer}

The answer of a source configuration of a coded machine after a deadline of
$t$ steps: the success tag $1$ followed by the accumulated output when the
machine has halted within $t$ steps, and the single timeout tag $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform completion of the timed interpreter]
\lean{Turing.timed_interpret_finishes}
\label{Turing.timed_interpret_finishes}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.CodeTM, Turing.CodeTM.serialize, Turing.MultiTapeTM.outputSymbol, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_output, Turing.timedAnswer, Turing.timedBorrow, Turing.timedBorrow_length, Turing.timedBorrow_value, Turing.timedCut_live_block, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timedLift, Turing.timedValue, Turing.timed_clock_success, Turing.timed_clock_timeout, Turing.timed_flush, Turing.timed_replay, Turing.universalSimulationCfg}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be a coded machine, let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite Boolean words, and let $r$ be
a natural number. For every configuration $\mathrm{src}$ of $M$ on input $x$, every
natural number $p$, and every finite Boolean word $bs$ such that $p\leq
|M.\mathrm{serialize}|$ and the little-endian value of $bs$ is $r$, there is a natural
number $d$ satisfying
\[
d\leq
\bigl(3|M.\mathrm{serialize}|+5(M.\mathrm{numStates}+1)+20+2|bs|+8\bigr)(r+1)+2|\mathrm{src.output}|,
\]
such that after $d$ steps the timed interpreter started from the six-tape lift of the
interpreter configuration for $M$, $\alpha$, $\mathrm{src}$, and $p$, with clock word
$bs$, is halted and its output is the deadline-inclusive answer for $\mathrm{src}$ after
$r$ steps of $M$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Five-lane assembly]
\lean{Turing.timedFive}
\label{Turing.timedFive}
\leanok
The assembly of a function on five tape indices from four core values and a
buffer value: indices $0$ through $3$ map to the core values (table, state,
simulated work, and input marker) and index $4$ to the buffer value.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Framed interpreter action]
\lean{Turing.timedFrameAction}
\label{Turing.timedFrameAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.FinTM, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.timedFive}
The lift of a six-tape timed-interpreter action to the assembled machine with
$k + 5$ tapes, for a base machine with $k$ tapes and a designated clock tape:
the action's clock component acts on the retained clock lane of the old block,
its remaining five components act on the five fresh lanes, and all other old
lanes are left untouched.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The capture wrapper]
\lean{Turing.timedCaptureTM}
\label{Turing.timedCaptureTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.timedFrameAction, Turing.timedInterpreter, Turing.timedSix}
The capture wrapper of a machine $M$ with a designated clock tape: it runs $M$
in lockstep while writing $M$'s emissions to a fresh table lane instead of the
output; when $M$ halts, control transfers to the timed interpreter, which runs
on the captured table, the retained clock lane, and four further fresh lanes.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[First-phase capture configuration]
\lean{Turing.timedCaptureCfg}
\label{Turing.timedCaptureCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks, Turing.timedCaptureTM}
The first-phase configuration of the capture wrapper corresponding to a
configuration of the base machine $M$: $M$'s tapes and heads are embedded, the
captured-table lane holds $M$'s accumulated output as a buffer with head at
its right blank, the remaining fresh lanes are blank, and the real output is
empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Capture wrapper initialization]
\lean{Turing.timedCapture_init}
\label{Turing.timedCapture_init}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.timedCaptureCfg, Turing.timedCaptureTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $i$ be one
of its work-tape indices, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean input. The capture machine
initialized on $x$ has exactly the configuration obtained by embedding $M$'s initial
configuration on $x$: its state is the embedded initial state, its original work tapes
and head positions are retained, its added buffer tape stores the initial output word
with its head at that word's length, its remaining added tapes are blank with heads at
zero, and its output is empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One captured step]
\lean{Turing.timedCapture_step}
\label{Turing.timedCapture_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.timedCaptureCfg, Turing.timedCaptureTM}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $c$ be one of its work
tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $C$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$
whose state is present. One step of the capture machine from the capture configuration
associated with $C$ equals the capture configuration associated with the result of one
step of $M$ from $C$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lockstep capture of a machine run]
\lean{Turing.timedCapture_run}
\label{Turing.timedCapture_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.timedCaptureCfg, Turing.timedCaptureTM, Turing.timedCapture_step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $i$ be one
of its work-tape indices, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, and let $c$ be a
configuration of $M$ on $x$. If $M$'s run from $c$ is not halted at any time $s<t$, then
after $t$ steps the capture machine started from the embedding of $c$ has exactly the
configuration obtained by embedding the configuration of $M$ after $t$ steps from $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Interpreter-entry capture configuration]
\lean{Turing.timedCapturedCfg}
\label{Turing.timedCapturedCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.timedCaptureCfg, Turing.timedCaptureTM, Turing.timedInterpreter}
The interpreter-entry configuration of the capture wrapper for a halted
configuration of the base machine: identical to its first-phase embedding
except that the finite control is the timed interpreter's initial state; the
retained clock lane becomes active again during interpretation.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Transfer from a halted configuration]
\lean{Turing.timedCapture_transfer}
\label{Turing.timedCapture_transfer}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.timedCaptureCfg, Turing.timedCaptureTM, Turing.timedCapturedCfg}
\difficulty{2}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $c$ be one of its work
tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $C$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. If
$C$ is halted, then one step of the capture machine from the capture configuration
associated with $C$ equals the interpreter-entry configuration associated with $C$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reaching the interpreter after capture]
\lean{Turing.timedCapture_start}
\label{Turing.timedCapture_start}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.timedCaptureTM, Turing.timedCapture_init, Turing.timedCapture_run, Turing.timedCapture_transfer, Turing.timedCapturedCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $c$ be one of its work
tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $T$ be a natural number. If the
configuration of $M$ after $T$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$ is halted,
then there is a time $t\le T+1$ at which the capture machine, started on $x$, is in the
interpreter-entry configuration associated with that time-$T$ configuration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Framed interpreter configuration]
\lean{Turing.timedFrame}
\label{Turing.timedFrame}

\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.timedCaptureTM, Turing.timedFive}
The configuration of the assembled capture machine determined by a six-tape
timed-interpreter configuration together with inactive tapes and heads for the
old block: the interpreter's clock lane is placed at the retained clock index
of the old block, its remaining five lanes occupy the fresh indices, and every
other old lane carries the given inactive data.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Reads of a Framed Configuration]
\lean{Turing.timedFrame_reads}
\label{Turing.timedFrame_reads}

Let $M$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine, choose a clock tape among its work
tapes, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. For any six-tape configuration $c$ and any
contents and head positions for the $M$ tapes, the six symbols read on the framed
configuration's four core tapes, clock tape, and buffer tape, assembled in that order,
equal the six symbols read from $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Applying a Framed Action]
\lean{Turing.timedFrame_apply}
\label{Turing.timedFrame_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.timedFive, Turing.timedFrame, Turing.timedFrameAction}

Let $M$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine, choose one of its work tapes as the
clock tape, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. For any six-tape configuration $c$,

applying the framed action to the framed configuration gives the frame of the

\begin{lemma}[One-step correspondence for framed configurations]
\lean{Turing.timedFrame_step}
\label{Turing.timedFrame_step}

\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_of_halt, Turing.TimedControl, Turing.timedCaptureTM, Turing.timedFrame, Turing.timedFrame_apply, Turing.timedFrame_reads, Turing.timedInterpreter}

its work-tape indices, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, and let $c$ be a six-tape

positions for the work tapes of $M$. Form a configuration of the capture machine by
keeping $c$’s input-head position and output, placing $c$’s fifth work tape in tape $j$,
and placing its other five work tapes in the five added tapes in their prescribed order;

configuration formed in the same way from the timed interpreter’s one-step successor of

\lean{Turing.timedFrame_run}
\label{Turing.timedFrame_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.TimedControl, Turing.timedCaptureTM, Turing.timedFrame, Turing.timedFrame_step, Turing.timedInterpreter}

Let $M$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine, choose a clock tape among its work
tapes, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. For every six-tape configuration $c$,

capture machine from the framed configuration for $t$ steps yields the frame of the
timed-interpreter run from $c$ for $t$ steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The captured entry is a frame]
\lean{Turing.timedCaptured_frame}
\label{Turing.timedCaptured_frame}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks, Turing.timedCaptureCfg, Turing.timedCapturedCfg, Turing.timedCut_InterpreterInitial, Turing.timedFive, Turing.timedFrame, Turing.timedLift, Turing.timedSix, Turing.universalFour}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $c$ be one of its work
tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $C$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$, and
let $b$ be a Boolean word. Suppose the contents of tape $c$ in $C$ are the buffer tape
holding $b$, and its head is at position $|b|$. Then the interpreter-entry capture

\begin{definition}[The timed universal machine]
\lean{Turing.timedUniversalTM}
\label{Turing.timedUniversalTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.FinTM, Turing.timedCanonClock, Turing.timedCanonTM, Turing.timedCaptureTM}
The complete timed universal machine of an effective coding scheme: the
capture wrapper of the composed clock-preserving canonizer, with its retained
clock lane.  It has finite control and finitely many tapes.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Code-only startup bound]
\lean{Turing.timedStartupBound}
\label{Turing.timedStartupBound}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM.serialize, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode}
The part of the timed universal machine's startup cost that depends only on
the code string $\alpha$: three times $|\alpha|$, plus the canonizer's time
bound at $|\alpha|$, plus the length of the decoded machine's serialization,
plus twice the width of its binary state count, plus twice its initial state
index, plus $16$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Header length within the serialization]
\lean{Turing.timed_header_bound}
\label{Turing.timed_header_bound}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM, Turing.CodeTM.serialize, Turing.universal_pair_length, Turing.universal_serialization_header}
\difficulty{2}
For every machine $M$ in code normal form, twice the number of bits in the binary
representation of its state-count parameter, plus $2$, plus its initial state index,
plus $1$, is at most the length of its canonical serialization.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Timed interpreter startup]
\lean{Turing.timed_initialized}
\label{Turing.timed_initialized}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM.serialize, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.timedCanonClock, Turing.timedCanonTM, Turing.timedCanon_complete, Turing.timedCaptureTM, Turing.timedCapture_start, Turing.timedCaptured_frame, Turing.timedCut_InterpreterBase, Turing.timedCut_InterpreterInitial, Turing.timedCut_Interpreter_initialize, Turing.timedFrame, Turing.timedFrame_run, Turing.timedLift, Turing.timedStartupBound, Turing.timedUniversalTM, Turing.timed_replay, Turing.universalEvalCfg, Turing.universalFour, Turing.universalInputPos, Turing.universalSimulationCfg, Turing.universal_pair_length, Turing.universal_serialization_header}
\difficulty{5}
Let $c$ be an effective machine coding scheme, and let $bs$, $\alpha$, and $x$ be
Boolean words. There exist a time $t$, work-tape contents, and work-tape head positions
for the auxiliary tapes such that $t \le 4|bs|+S_c(\alpha)$, where $S_c(\alpha)$ is the
timed startup bound for $c$ and $\alpha$, and the timed universal machine on input
$\langle\langle bs,\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$ is then in the configuration obtained by
lifting the decoded machine's initial configuration on $x$ to the timed interpreter,
with clock word $bs$ and table cursor $2|\operatorname{bin}(N)|+2+q+1$. Here $N$ is the
decoded machine's state-count parameter and $q$ is its initial-state index.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Quadratic cost bound]
\lean{Turing.timed_cost_bound}
\label{Turing.timed_cost_bound}

\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $S,B,t,w,s,d$, suppose $w\le t$, $s\le 4w+S$, and $d\le
(B+2w+8)(t+1)$. Then $s+d\le (S+B+14)(t+1)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Timed computation of a bounded answer]
\lean{Turing.timed_computes}
\label{Turing.timed_computes}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.length_bits_le_self, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.timedAnswer, Turing.timedCanonClock, Turing.timedCanonTM, Turing.timedCaptureTM, Turing.timedFrame, Turing.timedFrame_run, Turing.timedStartupBound, Turing.timedUniversalTM, Turing.timedValue_bits, Turing.timed_cost_bound, Turing.timed_header_bound, Turing.timed_initialized, Turing.timed_interpret_finishes, Turing.universalBlockBound}
\difficulty{4}
Let $c$ be an effective machine code, let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite Boolean strings,
and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. The timed universal machine, started on
$\langle\langle\operatorname{bin}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$, halts after exactly
$((S+B+14)(t+1)^2)$ steps and outputs $1$ followed by the decoded machine's output after
$t$ steps if that machine has halted by then; otherwise, it outputs the single bit $0$.
Here $S$ is the timed startup bound for $c,\alpha$, and $B$ is the block bound for
$c,\alpha$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Timed universal simulation with timeout]
\lean{Turing.timed_universal}
\label{Turing.timed_universal}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.timedAnswer, Turing.timedStartupBound, Turing.timedUniversalTM, Turing.timed_computes, Turing.universalBlockBound}
\difficulty{4}
For every effective machine coding scheme $c$, there is a finite-tape machine $U$ over
the Boolean alphabet such that for every Boolean code word $\alpha$ there is a natural
number $C$, and for every Boolean input $x$ and deadline $t$, both of the following
hold. If the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes an output $y$ on $x$ in exactly $t$
steps, then $U$ computes $1$ followed by $y$ on
$\langle\langle\operatorname{bin}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$ in exactly $C(t+1)^2$
steps; if it computes no output on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$ computes the
one-bit output $0$ on that input in exactly $C(t+1)^2$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\section{Additional declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Concrete timed simulation bound]
\lean{Turing.timed_universal_concrete}
\label{Turing.timed_universal_concrete}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM.serialize, Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.timedAnswer, Turing.timedUniversalTM, Turing.timed_computes, Turing.universalBlockBound}
\difficulty{4}
For every effective machine coding scheme $c$, there is a finite-tape machine $U$ over
the Boolean alphabet such that for every Boolean code word $\alpha$, Boolean input $x$,
and natural number $t$, both of the following hold. Write $L$ for the length of the
canonical serialization of the machine decoded from $\alpha$, $N$ for its state-count
parameter, $q$ for its initial-state index, and $T(n)$ for the canonizer's time bound.
If the decoded machine computes output $y$ on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$
computes $1$ followed by $y$ on
$\langle\langle\operatorname{bin}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$ in exactly
$C_{c,\alpha}(t+1)^2$ steps; if it computes no output on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then
$U$ computes the one-bit output $0$ on that input in exactly the same number of steps,
where
$C_{c,\alpha}=(3|\alpha|+T(|\alpha|)+L+2|\operatorname{bin}(N)|+2q+16)+(3L+5(N+1)+20)+14$.
\end{theorem}
